AN ORDINANCE TO AMEND THE WATER ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF ARNOLDSVILLE, GEORGIA, ENTITLED “CITY OF ARNOLDSVILLE WATER ORDINANCE EFFECTIVE JANUARY 1, 1994", AS AMENDED

The Mayor and Council of the City of Arnoldsville, Georgia hereby ordains as follows:
1:
of the charter of the City of Arnoldsville, (Ga. Laws 1969, p. 3248), the water ordinance of the City of Arnoldsville, Georgia as previously amended is hereby amended as follows:

Request for water service from the Arnoldsville Water Department must be made by application for the purpose of establishing customer’s name, mailing address, placement of meter, and type use for rate classification.

The City Council may adjust any of the fees, costs, procedures and any other matter dealing with the water system and the delivery of water in the exercise of proper maintenance and financial solvency of the water system. Said adjustments may be made by ordinance, resolution or administratively. Any changes made to any fees, costs, procedures and any other matters dealing with the water system, other than by ordinance, shall be posted to the City website by the City Clerk within 48 hours of their adoption by the City. Copies of this Ordinance and any adjustments to any of the fees, costs, procedures and any other matter dealing the water system shall be made available to the public upon request.

l, Meters.

Each individual resident dwelling, commercial building or business must have its own meter. (Mayor and council shall be empowered to determine what constitutes a resident dwelling, commercial building, and business.)

Mobile Home Parks are to have one meter for each section of the park. (Mayor and Council shall be empowered to determine what constitutes a Mobile Home Park and the number of sections which make up the Park.)

2: Ownership and Maintenance.

The City of Arnoldsville shall own, place, replace, and maintain all parts of the water system from the water source, through the water main, up to the meter and the meter. The customer shall own and maintain that part from the meter on.

Water customers are responsible for damages to water meters that may occur from grass cutting or other outside activities. As a result of lawn mower damage etc., numerous water meters have to be replaced by the city each spring and summer.

Replacement charges for these damages including labor as adopted by the city are as follows:

ee Tap-on to Water Main

Tap-on fees Inside City Limits will be $600.00. Tap-on fees Outside City Limits will be $1,100.00. Tap-on fees are subject to change, based on the economy. An unauthorized tap-on will be subject to a fine of $500.00. A fee to be determined by the City Council, but no less than $450.00 will be charged if a bore is required to connect to the City Water System. Tap-on fees are required at the time of application for water service.

4, Non-Refundable Application Fee

. Each new water customer at the time of applying for water service shall pay a nonrefundable Application Fee of $125.00.

5; Water Rates.

A. Water rates may be adjusted by the Mayor and Council as they may deem fit and necessary in order for the water system to be self-supporting for immediate cash flow and anticipated infrastructure maintenance.

B. Commercial usage shall be dealt with on an individual basis by Mayor and Council. Mobile Home Parks are classified as commercial.

- 6. Non-payment. Payment made after due date must include a 10% late fee. If payment for water bill is not received within 30 days of due date, a written warning will be issued to person responsible for bill. If payment is not received within 60 days of due date, the meter will be locked. To receive service again, the water bill must be paid in full plus the reconnection fee of $50.00. A $100.00 reconnection fee will be charged for a second and/or subsequent reconnection for non-payment of water bill(s), t, Notice to Discontinue. It is the responsibility of property owner, as well as the water customer, to notify City five days prior to discontinuing service.

- 8. Conservation.

It is the duty of each person to use water as the precious resource that it is by immediately repairing leaky plumbing on their premises and report any leaks or other waste of water from city mains.

9, Water Shortage or Scarcity:

- 1. In any case of a water shortage or scarcity, the Mayor and Council may restrict the use of water.

- 2. A violation of any established restriction of water will result in a written warning; if said violation continues, a verbal warning by Mayor and a Council person or a law enforcement officer; if still continued, the meter will be removed, and a reconnection fee of $50.00 will be charged to restore service.

- 10. Water Rate Scale.

- 1. Inside city limits - residential:

0-3,000 gallons, $18.00 (minimum charge), plus $3.00 for each additional 1,000 gallons or part thereof for 3,000 to 5,999 gallons plus $4.00 for each additional 1,000 gallons, or part thereof over 6,000 gallons, per month.
